correctness.rationale: A fixed geometric point has constant barycentric weights on each coordinate-rotation orbit, giving an exact PL orbit-complex model. Summing rotation Hamming distances gives 2w(k-w), and since nontrivial shifts contribute at most 2 each, for k>=4 only block weights 0,1,k-1,k are possible. Explicit exhaustive type-wise cross-orbit distances give two disconnected layers, each obtained from VR(Q_m;2) by coning off the radius-one simplex about each of its vertices. A simplicial retraction sends each cone tip to its central base vertex; identity and retraction are contiguous on every simplex, producing a strong deformation retract. This proves all quantified cases, including m=0 and k=4. The prior Adamaszek-Adams integral homotopy theorem yields the claimed component sphere count. A standalone exhaustive orbit-and-pair consistency check passed 19 parameter combinations, 300 admissible orbit vertices, and 4274 pairs; finite checks support but do not prove the quantified theorem.

value.rationale: The fixed-point topology of a natural coordinate-cycle subgroup is a genuine geometric equivariant invariant not determined by rational homology characters or ordinary ambient Betti numbers. A uniform all-long-cycle classification exhibits a sharp change from the previously studied short rotation types to two disconnected persistent three-sphere-wedge components, and supplies an explicit strong retraction instead of a homological Euler count. This answers a natural structural question for an infinite family, not an arbitrary graph-by-graph enumeration. The question of hyperoctahedral equivariant Rips cohomology is explicitly motivated in arXiv:2408.17331, Question 8; the computed subgroup geometric fixed loci furnish concrete relevant data, without claiming to solve the broader question.
